the clearance of inhaled arsenic and antimony compounds is influenced by the chemical form of the compound.
inhaled arsenic dusts are cleared from lungs more rapidly than are antimony dusts.
antimony is retained in the lung for a long period of time after inhalation exposure to industrial dust.

the retention and clearance of antimony and antimony compounds in the lung.
the retention in the lungs of inhaled dust particles containing arsenic and antimony.
the retention of antimony in the hamster lung following intratracheal administration of factory dust and antimony compounds.

the solubility in saline and the biological half-times were the most important parameters for the retention of antimony tri-oxide and arsenic tri-oxide in the hamster lung.
the solubility is a more important factor in the lung retention of antimony than the particle size, while for arsenic the reverse is the case.
the retention of antimony in the lung is greater than the retention of arsenic in the lung.

the lung retention of antimony in workers exposed to factory dust is probably related to the low solubility and long biological half-time of antimony.
